messages:
Maya: Heads-up — running a simulated incident tomorrow 09:00 PDT onprem-nyc cluster. Scope: RBAC emergency escalation, KMS key failover (Vault backed), and audit pipeline (filebeat -> SIEM). Need one oncall + one infra to run the play.
Simon: I can take oncall for the window. Happy to help run the KMS failover steps.
Raj: Quick Q — are we exercising netpol isolation too or just RBAC/KMS/audit? I want to validate egress whitelisting under load.
Maya: Both. Test plan: 1) escalate a service-account to emergency-role (simulated least-privilege breach) 2) rotate/disable a Vault key and failover to standby 3) ensure network policies block unexpected egress and audit events hit SIEM within 60s.
Elaine: FYI from pentest bench — found a misconfig in vault-proxy where the agent forwarded metadata requests from node to Vault with elevated token. Triage note: this only affects older telemetry-agent <2.2.0.
Olivia: Which clusters run the vulnerable agent?
Elaine: onprem-nyc and onprem-sfo have 2.1.x. Staging already at 2.2.1.
Jordan: We should block the test on production-like nodes until agent is patched. If we must test rotation, do it in staging first and cut network access on the vulnerable nodes.
Maya: Agreed. Patch timeline: Olivia will coordinate agent rollout tonight. Simon + Raj — run the RBAC escalation and KMS failover in staging at 02:00, then dry-run in canary onprem-nyc 06:00 before the 09:00 sim.
Olivia: On it. I'll push agent 2.2.1 to onprem-nyc canary group at 23:00.
Simon: Can someone paste the exact commands for vault key disable/rollover? Want to codify in runbook.
Elaine: Rollover snippet (Vault HSM):
```
# snapshot current key
vault write transit/keys/redwood-inference/rotate
# disable current signer (soft disable)
vault write transit/keys/redwood-inference disabled=true
# promote standby
vault write transit/keys/redwood-inference-promote promote=true
```
Note: our Vault is wrapped behind internal auth proxy; don't run raw API calls without the proxy token.
Raj: For RBAC escalation test, use ephemeral elevation via our oauth-approver: `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:infra:emergency --namespace=default get secrets` then validate audit event shows `user.identity=oauth-approver`.
Maya: Audit config we want on for the test (kube-apiserver audit-policy.yaml snippet):
```
apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1
kind: Policy
rules:
- level: RequestResponse
  users: ["system:serviceaccount:infra:emergency"]
  verbs: ["create","delete","patch"]
  resources:
  - group: ""
    resources: ["secrets","configmaps"]
```
And ensure `--audit-log-path=/var/log/kube-audit/audit.log` with rotation and filebeat monitoring.
Olivia: SIEM mapping: tag events with `env=onprem-nyc, test=rbac-kms-drill, incident=INC-2026-0412` so the incident dashboard filters work. I'll add the mapping in filebeat config.
sec-bot: New incident created INC-2026-0412 (severity: low) — playbook: /ops/runbooks/onprem-kms-rbac-drill.md
Jordan: NetworkPolicy sample to enforce egress whitelisting during test (apply on the app namespace):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-whitelist-test
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/16    # internal services
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: telemetry
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
This blocks all other egress by default.
Simon: For rollback if something goes sideways:
- re-enable original vault key: `vault write transit/keys/redwood-inference disabled=false`
- revoke emergency SA tokens: `kubectl delete token emergency-*-token -n infra`
- restore audit-policy from `s3://runbooks/audit-policy-backup.yaml`
Maya: Also add a quick check list to confirm audit ingestion: `curl http://siem-ingest.internal/_search?q=test:rbac-kms-drill` should return events within 60s.
Raj: We also need to exercise the fallback routing for model-serving nodes — if KMS rotates, clients should accept the new key thumbprint. Who owns that code path?
Elaine: Runtime team — ping @Jordan to validate client key caching TTL is <= 5m for the test.
Jordan: I'll add a temporary TTL override in the configmap and roll restart the serving pods before the simulation.
Olivia: Quick security extra: ensure node egress to metadata endpoint is blocked for anything not running node-proxy:
```
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 169.254.169.254 -j DROP
```
We'll apply via kube-proxy daemonset on the vulnerable nodes.
Simon: Sounds good. Anything else on detection? We should ensure alerting rules are enabled: filebeat -> SIEM -> PagerDuty path.
Maya: Alerting ON. PagerDuty escalation set to two engineers then sec-manager.
Raj: Question on logs: retention for this test — keep full audit logs for 30d in cold storage and 7d hot. Is that in place?
Olivia: Yes, filebeat pipeline sends to hot index `audit-hot-*` 7d then roll to `audit-cold-*` 30d. I'll confirm index lifecycle policy.
Elaine: One more triage note — the pentest also flagged a path where a job could mount `hostPath: /var/run/secrets` in older kubelet configs. That was patched two months ago but double-check hostPath admission plugin is enabled in canary.
Maya: Thanks — action items summarized: Olivia: agent rollout + filebeat tag; Simon+Raj: run RBAC + KMS failover tests in staging then canary; Jordan: TTL override and hostPath admission check; Elaine: confirm Vault proxy token flows and pentest remediation; I'll run the sim at 09:00 PDT and coordinate console updates.
Simon: :thumbsup:
Olivia: Will post a quick runbook link when agent rollout is done.
sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-0412 updated: status=preparing, runbook=/ops/runbooks/onprem-kms-rbac-drill.md
Maya: If anyone sees anything unexpected during the test, @Maya @Simon please escalate to PagerDuty immediately and annotate the SIEM incident.
Raj: Noted. See you all tomorrow.
